title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1967-05-05
lineage: SBD > unknown analog gens > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Good‑quality early board/audience capture of a fiery ’67 set – crisp Golden Road → New Potato Caboose → Alligator with solid playing despite some bass‑saturation and occasional muddiness.
ai_review.review: The recording preserves one of the rare mid‑'60s snapshots where the Dead blaze through Golden Road, New Potato Caboose and Alligator with exuberant banter and tight improvisation.  While the tape suffers from a slightly over‑saturated low end and occasional vocal mud‑iness, listeners repeatedly praise Jerry’s searing lead, Phil’s hot bass, Pigpen’s organ whirl and the overall youthful energy of the performance.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews are 4‑5 stars and focus on outstanding musical moments; recording flaws are noted but not enough to outweigh the show’s historic value.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early era tape – generally clear enough to hear each instrument, but bass is a bit over‑saturated, vocals can be muddy and occasional drop‑outs are mentioned. Still considered one of the better available recordings from this transitional period.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend Of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: A short, high‑energy four‑song set that rolls seamlessly from Golden Road into New Potato Caboose and then Alligator; the banter adds historic flavor.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers note his fiery guitar tone, soaring solos and overall fire in this era.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass is repeatedly described as “hot”, “on fire” and a driving force behind the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Several comments praise the three‑part vocal harmonies of Jerry, Bob and Phil.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ work gets high marks – described as amazing, whizzing, B3‑like and adding warmth to the set.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann (sometimes referred to as Bill Summers) is praised for artistic drumming; a few note that two‑drummer setups can muddy the mix but his playing remains solid.
